subject: Integration: PromptGuard SDK -> Redwood runtime (proposal)
messages:
From: Liz Patel <liz@promptguard.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: PromptGuard Engineering <eng@promptguard.io>, Partnerships <partnerships@promptguard.io>
Date: 2025-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Integration: PromptGuard SDK -> Redwood runtime (proposal)

Hi Irene —

Great to reconnect after last week's partner briefing. PromptGuard has built a lightweight SDK that adds real-time prompt instrumentation, policy checks, and prompt-editing helpers to the developer flow. We believe a native integration with Redwood's runtime (for tracing, safe defaults, and optional execution routing) would be a high-value partner offering for ISV customers using LangChain/LlamaIndex.

Attached is a short proposal that outlines two integration modes:
- In-line SDK hooks that call Redwood's hosted inference for policy-evaluated prompts
- Out-of-band tracing + telemetry that forwards request metadata to Redwood for aggregated analytics and causal tracing

Key asks from our side:
1) Compatibility with Redwood's streaming responses and function-calling protocol
2) Support for carrying tracing headers (X-Request-ID / Redwood-Trace) end-to-end
3) A small dedicated test environment (sandbox) for SDK customers to validate end-to-end flows

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical sync next week? Attaching the proposal (promptguard-redwood-proposal.pdf) and a one-pager.

Thanks — excited to explore this with you.

--
Liz Patel
Head of Partnerships | PromptGuard
liz@promptguard.io
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: promptguard-redwood-proposal.pdf (pdf, 350KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Patel <liz@promptguard.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-15T10:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration: PromptGuard SDK -> Redwood runtime (proposal)

Thanks Liz — appreciate the crisp proposal. I looped in Jonas (runtime/inference) and Marissa (ecosystem/partner ops) so we can scope feasibility and next steps.

Top-level responses:
- Streaming & function-calling: Redwood supports both; we'll need to validate the SDK's approach to chunked token flushing and how it expects function call payloads to be surfaced.
- Tracing headers: we can pass and propagate X-Request-ID and Redwood-Trace through our routing layer. We usually recommend a 64-bit trace id + client-generated nonce for correlation.
- Sandbox: we have a small partner sandbox (Redwood Partner Sandbox) we can provision. It has limited throughput but is perfect for SDK validation.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jonas: review the proposal and mark any red flags in the attached checklist (redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx).
2) PromptGuard: share sample SDK hook snippets and a minimal call flow (headers, payload).
3) Marissa: create a partner workspace and HubSpot record if we proceed (cc'd).

Can we tentatively book Wed 2025-11-19 10:00 PT for a 45-min tech session? If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and the sandbox access details.

Thanks — Irene

--
Irene Choi
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB); security-questions.pdf (pdf, 48KB)
From: Liz Patel <liz@promptguard.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: PromptGuard Engineering <eng@promptguard.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-17T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration: PromptGuard SDK -> Redwood runtime (proposal)

Irene / team —

Thanks, Jonas/Marissa for jumping in. Per your checklist we put together a short tech appendix and some code snippets (sdk-hook-snippets.txt). Highlights:
- Hook model: SDK wraps the LLM client and emits a pre-send hook (prompt, metadata) and a post-receive hook (tokens, deltas, final). Pre-send can call an external policy endpoint; post-receive can stream deltas back to host.
- Headers: we surface X-Request-ID and X-PromptGuard-Trace; we can mirror Redwood's Redwood-Trace header if you prefer.
- Streaming: the SDK supports both SSE and chunked HTTP streaming. For function-calls we surface a single function payload once all tokens are received; we can also emit partial function args in the post-receive hook for long-running responses.
- Authentication: OAuth2 bearer for customer sandbox; mutual TLS possible for enterprise integrations.

Attached: sdk-hook-snippets.txt. Also linked a short Loom recording showing the SDK flow.

We can confirm Wed 2025-11-19 10:00 PT for the tech session. If you prefer a brief pre-read, we'll share a sandbox demo account today.

Best,
Liz

Attachments: sdk-hook-snippets.txt (txt, 6KB)
Related links: https://loom.com/share/promptguard-sdk-flow
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Liz Patel <liz@promptguard.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-18T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration: PromptGuard SDK -> Redwood runtime (proposal)

Thanks for the details, Liz — helpful appendix. A few quick technical clarifications before the sync:

1) Streaming deltas: can the SDK emit token-level deltas with stable sequence IDs so we can reconstruct partial outputs in our tracing UI? We prefer an incremental id (sequence_num) + chunk_hash per delta.
2) Function-calls: you mentioned emitting a final function payload — does the SDK provide a deterministic boundary marker for when function output is "final" vs. provisional?
3) Trace context: we'll forward Redwood-Trace plus client-provided X-Request-ID; can the SDK accept an incoming Redwood-Trace and continue it (i.e., inject into subsequent internal telemetry)? That unlocks cross-system trace joins.
4) Sandbox quotas: Marissa — can you provision the Partner Sandbox with 5 concurrent connections and 100k tokens/day for PromptGuard (email the creds to liz@promptguard.io)?

If we get short answers to 1-3 today we can focus the sync on demoing the end-to-end flow and SSO/auth. Agenda for Wed: 1) quick architecture (10m), 2) live demo (20m), 3) integration checklist & next milestones (15m).

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
